reading.body:
This Orangeburg campus near the New Jersey border, about 22 miles from Manhattan, occupies 232,000 square feet today with planned expansion to 462,000 square feet on a 23-acre site. The operator publishes 12 MW on-site today and states a substation capacity for up to 50 MW total, but does not publish a single unambiguous current critical IT load figure, so the effective capacity available to AI workloads cannot be determined from public sources.

If the 12 MW on-site figure represents current critical IT load, this assumes 1.2 MW per 100,000 square feet of current building, a low utilization rate that could accommodate substantial expansion. The operator supports high-density cabinets at 10 kW and above, and 12 network providers serve the site. Scaling from typical hyperscale GPU cluster densities of roughly 8 MW per 100 racks, 12 MW of IT load would supply approximately 150 racks, though this is an assumption about utilization that the operator does not state.

In New York, where only one facility of 31 mapped publishes megawatts at all, this campus ranks second by published MW in the state and represents one-quarter of the 3 MW of total published capacity announced. The low denominator reflects how rarely data center operators disclose power figures; this campus's publication is an exception.
